f4b4bb981e:45ba4d56110252b6.title: Global Digital Collaboration Conference
f4b4bb981e:45ba4d56110252b6.summary: Visual identity for the Global Digital Collaboration Conference 2026 in Geneva. GDC brings together governments, international organisations, technology companies and other stakeholders to collaborate on the digital infrastructure and standards that increasingly connect our world. At the heart of the identity is the Global Barcode, an idea conceived by GDC founder Daniel Goldscheider. It translates the flags of all UN member states into simple vertical colour codes, based on the colours and their proportions within each national flag. Put together, they form one global code. And one very, very long flag. This became the starting point for the visual identity: an endless flag that folds, bends and winds its way through posters, spaces, shirts, lanyards and the conference itself. For the participant badges, the principle became personal: each name generates its own individual colour code.

f4b4bb981e:eaf91ce84cda68fb.title: Bradesco - São João
f4b4bb981e:eaf91ce84cda68fb.summary: We were invited by Lovely to create this São João campaign for Bradesco, inspired by the friendly rivalry between Caruaru and Campina Grande, home to two of Brazil's biggest June festivals. Building on the campaign concept, we developed a visual language inspired by Northeastern Brazilian folk culture and the tradition of repente, a form of improvised poetic dueling built around rhymes, wit, and playful provocation. We created a series of handcrafted illustrations that bring these two cities together, exploring the colors, shapes, and visual elements associated with São João celebrations. Each composition was designed to capture the spirit of rivalry while also celebrating a sense of unity. The result is a series of pieces that turn rivalry into connection and visually express the campaign's central message: the greatest São João is the one we create together.

f4b4bb981e:ec58b8cd447803b8.title: FoundersCard
f4b4bb981e:ec58b8cd447803b8.summary: FoundersCard has built a unique proposition around access?connecting an ambitious community of entrepreneurs and business leaders with exceptional benefits, experiences, and opportunities. Our challenge was to create a digital experience that felt as considered and valuable as the membership itself. We began by rethinking the experience from the ground up. Stripping away complexity, sharpening the hierarchy, and creating a clearer way to communicate the breadth of the FoundersCard world. The goal was simple: make something premium without feeling exclusive for the sake of it, and sophisticated without becoming complicated. A new visual language brought that thinking to life. Bold typography, confident layouts, elevated imagery, and a more editorial approach gave the brand greater presence and personality. A flexible design system created consistency across the experience while leaving room for partners, benefits, destinations, and stories to each have their own moment.

f4b4bb981e:3875c0ab30f5f488.title: Tron: Ares ? Computer Vision
f4b4bb981e:3875c0ab30f5f488.summary: What does perception look like when it belongs to a machine? That question became the foundation for our work on TRON: Ares, where our team of twenty artists designed and animated more than sixty shots of computer vision and interface systems that visualize the world through the eyes of Ares. Rather than creating traditional HUD graphics, we set out to design machine perception itself. Every frame exists as a living system that continuously scans, tracks, evaluates, and reconstructs reality as streams of computation. Driven by a philosophy of maximum detail, each live action plate was transformed through our custom squarepacking algorithms into a computational lattice capable of analyzing the image at multiple scales simultaneously. Source code, reactive graphics, tracking systems, and layered analysis become different expressions of the same intelligence, revealing a world where every pixel is continuously interpreted and every image is rewritten through the language of the machine.

f4b4bb981e:abb39fac635e1988.title: BLASTEMA
f4b4bb981e:abb39fac635e1988.summary: A blastema is the tissue a body forms to regenerate something it has lost. It is made up of progenitor cells capable, for a time, of changing state and giving rise to something else. They don't have a fixed form yet. They are going to become something different. This project starts there and pushes the idea into a place where biology no longer applies: insects whose tissue, instead of regenerating as insects, begins to behave like plant matter. Lichens, moss, mycelium, fungal fruiting bodies. They are not placed on top. They grow from the same tissue, as if the cell had switched sides. The process: each specimen begins as an image, is reconstructed in 3D, and ultimately becomes a Gaussian Splat rendered in real time through our own GLSL shaders. This is where it truly comes alive. It is no longer a fixed model, but a structure that scatters light and changes according to the viewpoint.

a4977d3fa4:369b81086e15128d.title: Inside Brooklyn’s Most Electric NYFW Event Celebrating Public School and WHATMORE for Our September Covers
a4977d3fa4:369b81086e15128d.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:369b81086e15128d.summary: New York Fashion Week kicked off with an undeniable surge of energy as Hypebeast brought its editorial pages to life for our Digital Cover celebration at Brooklyn’s 99 Scott. The evening brought together two generations of New York creative talent to celebrate our September cover stars: iconic streetwear pioneers Dao-Yi Chow and Maxwell Osborne of Public School, alongside the rising five-piece music group WHATMORE. Transforming the industrial warehouse space into an authentic block party, the night honored the city's multi-hyphenate mindset—where fashion, music, and urban culture naturally intersect.Serving as the seamless thread throughout the venue, Toyota’s all-electric C-HR was integrated directly into the rhythm of the event. The vehicle functioned as an interactive hub for attendees. Guests climbed into the backseat of the all-electric C-HR to record raw "car confessionals" and snap high-energy photo booth shots framed with custom event artwork. Adding an element of play, guests were handed branded keychains upon entry, testing their luck to unlock an in-car lockbox stocked with a curated road-trip style tote filled with Public School merch and JBL speakers.The physical environment tapped into classic New York iconography, featuring a custom newsstand-inspired merch booth set up in the center of the space. In a direct nod to the September digital covers, the booth served limited-edition "No Tricks in '26" graphic tees designed by Public School. Styled in the visual language of vintage newsprint, the shirts were handed out to guests straight from street-vendor racks and clear newspaper dispensers, turning the distribution of ephemera into a memorable design moment.Music powered the atmosphere from start to finish, keeping the crowd engaged throughout the three-hour gathering. Blu DeTiger set the initial tone from the DJ booth with an electric set while attendees enjoyed curated bites from culinary collective Ghetto Gastro. The marquee moment arrived when…

a4977d3fa4:b6ea33a501bb3f9a.title: Inside Hypebeast Afterhours: A Saul Nash LFW Afterparty at Soho House
a4977d3fa4:b6ea33a501bb3f9a.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:b6ea33a501bb3f9a.summary: The latest Hypebeast Afterhours hit London last weekend, hosted in collaboration with designer, dancer and choreographer Saul Nash.Hot off the heels of the NYFW edition, the event took place during London Fashion Week at Soho House’s 180 House, with views overlooking the city’s lit-up skyline.With attendees pulling up in their best fits for the late-night event, cocktails were provided by Grey Goose and sounds were spun by Miles Peart, Cktrl, and Saul Nash himself, which brought the energy well into the early hours of Sunday,The Hypebeast x Saul Nash party came hours after the designer showcased his latest collection “Masquerade” at a pop-up installation inside the Dray Walk gallery. Inside, pieces originally shown on the runway at Milan Fashion Week were available to buy ahead of their general launch, with mood boards, design processes, and references from the season all on display for passersby to see.Also on view was a hand-picked curation of art from Gray Wielebinski and Izaak Brandt, alongside magazines, books, and other material that had inspired Nash this season. “Masquerade in Residence is a chance for people to step inside our world and interact with the clothing up close," Nash explains. "Although it is only going to be there for a few days, it is more than just a typical pop-up shop. It is an opportunity to invite London and my community into the brand’s world”.Take a look at the gallery to see what went down. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:c1d839a606daee91.title: Heinz’s Simply Spicy and Simply Pickle Ketchup Bring Real Jalapeños and Briny Tang to a Cleaner Recipe
a4977d3fa4:c1d839a606daee91.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:c1d839a606daee91.summary: Summary Heinz has launched Simply Spicy Ketchup and Simply Pickle Ketchup, the first flavored additions to its Simply lineupBoth varieties rework the brand's best-selling flavored ketchups around a simplified ingredient listSimply Spicy gets its heat from real jalapeños, while Simply Pickle layers a tangy, briny profile over Heinz's signature tomato base Heinz has introduced Simply Spicy Ketchup and Simply Pickle Ketchup, expanding its Simply line with its first flavored varieties. Both build on the stripped-back recipe philosophy behind the original Simply ketchup and bring it to two of the brand's most popular flavor profiles.The foundation is the original Heinz Simply ketchup, which uses just seven real ingredients and contains no artificial colors, flavors, sweeteners or preservatives. Heinz says the recipe keeps the thick, rich texture its classic ketchup is known for, so the shorter ingredient list doesn't come at the cost of consistency. The new flavors take cues from Heinz's top-selling flavored ketchups and rebuild them to fit the same simplified standard.Simply Spicy blends ripe red tomatoes with spices and real jalapeños, relying on actual peppers for its heat rather than a flavoring shortcut. Heinz pitches it as an all-purpose kick for burgers, chicken and even scrambled eggs.Simply Pickle keeps Heinz's familiar tomato base and adds a bright, briny pickle flavor for a sharper, tangier finish. It's aimed at the classic ketchup pairings, including hot dogs, fries and sandwiches, where a hit of acidity cuts through richer foods.The timing tracks with shifting shopper habits. Heinz cites figures showing that two in three shoppers actively look for simple, recognizable ingredient lists, while 85% say taste remains a priority when choosing food. On the flavor side, the brand points to 95% of consumers reporting that they enjoy hot and spicy foods in 2026, and year-over-year category sales growth of more than 30% for pickle-flavored products.Heinz Simply…

a4977d3fa4:c0c9cae0ec33f3ee.title: Adam Driver, Miles Teller, and Scarlett Johansson Star in Official Trailer for James Gray's 'Paper Tiger'

a4977d3fa4:c0c9cae0ec33f3ee.summary: Summary Neon has debuted the official trailer for 'Paper Tiger' written and directed by James GrayThe 1980s crime drama stars Adam Driver Miles Teller and Scarlett Johansson as a family entangled with the Russian mafiaFollowing its premiere at the Cannes Film Festival the film will open the New York Film Festival ahead of its November release Neon has released the official trailer for Paper Tiger, an upcoming 1980s crime drama written and directed by James Gray. The film stars Adam Driver, Miles Teller, and Scarlett Johansson in a story centered on family, crime, and the American Dream.Set in 1986 Queens, New York, the plot follows brothers Gary (Driver), an ex-cop, and Isaac (Teller), an engineer. When Gary draws his brother into a scheme that entangles them with the Russian mafia, their family's safety and survival are put at risk. Johansson stars as Isaac's wife, who faces her own turmoil as the scheme unfolds. Gray noted that the narrative draws loose inspiration from his own family's encounter with the Russian mafia in 1980s New York City.The film made its world premiere in competition at the Cannes Film Festival in May 2026, earning a 10-minute standing ovation following its screening. Acquired by Neon prior to its Cannes debut, the project is scheduled to open the New York Film Festival at the end of September.Paper Tiger begins its limited theatrical run on November 13, 2026. a4977d3fa4:d6afa33599ebdb31.title: On Reveals Plans to Launch Golf and Football Categories as It Targets $7 Billion USD in 2029 Sales
a4977d3fa4:d6afa33599ebdb31.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:d6afa33599ebdb31.summary: Summary Swiss sportswear brand outlines 2029 targets approaching $7 billion in absolute net salesExpansions into golf and football product ranges are officially slated for early 2027Strategic shift to U.S. dollar reporting will align financials with actual business economics Swiss sportswear powerhouse On revealed its plan to disrupt the country club during its investor day at the Zurich headquarters on Tuesday. Executives laid out a three-year growth plan to secure 2029 ambitions. The brand is mapping its evolution as a publicly traded company by entering major global sports. Co-chief executive officer Caspar Coppetti announced that the label will add a golf category to its roster in early 2027. Internal backing for the move includes chief design officer Thilo Brunner and president Scott Maguire, who are both avid golfers. Tennis icon Roger Federer attended the event to express excitement for the extension into the golf space.Football represents another arena receiving the Swiss treatment following a recent partnership with superstar Kylian Mbappé. Linking with the French forward generated $8 billion USD in earned media reach, according to founder and co-chief executive officer David Allemann. This cultural alignment shifts the demographic younger, as 72 percent of followers gained since the announcement are under the age of 35. Digital momentum supports the upcoming release of the first On Football product range in 2027. Diversifying into these segments moves the company from a specialized running label into a multi-sport powerhouse capable of sustaining momentum on the public market.The Zurich-based label established specific financial targets for the road to 2029 to support its expansion. The patent depicts a sophisticated dual-clutch transmission that defies conventional design by incorporating both a physical clutch pedal and a traditional gear shifter. This development directly addresses a massive industry challenge of preserving the visceral feel of a manual transmission as modern powertrains evolve. By designing a system that visually and mechanically bridges the gap between old-school engagement and modern performance, the manufacturer is preparing to offer driving purists a lifeline in the hybrid era.During standard operation, the setup functions identically to a normal automatic transmission and allows for effortless cruising without the need to work three pedals. When drivers want to dictate the shifting rhythm without fully committing to a manual experience, they can choose to shift through the gears manually using paddle shifters mounted directly on the steering wheel. The system provides another tactile option in automatic mode by allowing the driver to select gears through shifting the center gear selector backward and forward. a4977d3fa4:08c0386ae3dc7b2f.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:08c0386ae3dc7b2f.summary: Summary Bungie is reversing its six-year-old 'Destiny Content Vault' to restore previously removed campaigns, destinations and raids to the gameDevelopers must completely update the older content's lighting and underlying systems to match modern stability standards before reintroductionThe massive course correction arrives just weeks after fans launched a rogue offline preservation mod to access locked areas Bungie is officially walking back one of the most controversial decisions in modern gaming history. Three months after releasing the final update for Destiny 2, the studio announced plans to reverse its six-year-old Destiny Content Vault. This massive pivot will fully restore previously removed campaigns, destinations and raids to the live game, with all players receiving access to the returning content. Outlined in a blog post authored by studio head Poria Torkan and head of product Josh Deane, the move directly addresses an era of the shooter that stripped away older content players had originally paid cash to access.The timing of this reversal coincides with recent community efforts to save the history of the game. Bungie announced the decision weeks after the release of an offline preservation mod named Sunrise. While that fan-made toolkit allowed players to load into vaulted areas, it did not contain the exact campaigns and missions players had experienced previously. Official restoration work will take substantial time because developers must update the older content’s lighting, encounters, combatants and underlying systems. These heavy systemic updates are required because of major engine changes made during the Beyond Light expansion. Reintroducing these environments ensures they meet current stability and gameplay standards.This un-vaulting operates as a massive structural fix and serves as an effort to salvage community goodwill at a critical cultural juncture. a4977d3fa4:8148c252dfe1b699.summary: Summary SteelSeries has added limited Cyber and Steel editions to its Apex Pro TKL Gen 3 keyboard lineup as part of its 25th anniversaryNew OmniPoint 3.0 switch options come in two spring weights, Speed and Control, for a more tailored keystroke feelThe boards run on SteelSeries' Gen 3 Hall Effect sensing and its Triple Threat suite of Rapid Trigger, Protection Mode and Rapid Tap SteelSeries has introduced the Apex Pro TKL Gen 3 Cyber and Steel, a pair of limited-edition keyboards that expand the brand's flagship magnetic-switch line with new switch options. Rather than relying on software alone to change how a board responds, the new weights let players choose a physical feel that matches their playstyle before any settings are touched.Beneath each key is what SteelSeries calls the industry's first Hall Effect Gen 3 sensor, which the brand markets with an "S-Tier" label. Hall Effect switches read key position magnetically instead of through physical contact, which allows actuation points to be measured and adjusted with fine precision. SteelSeries positions the Apex Pro line as the world's fastest gaming keyboards, and the Gen 3 sensing is the foundation of that claim.Acoustics and feel get attention as well. a4977d3fa4:54f3e086953b01ea.title: What If You Could Buy Your Vintage Denim Brand New?

a4977d3fa4:54f3e086953b01ea.summary: Not all denim is created equal. Fit, wash, texture, construction...there’s a laundry list of details separating a decent pair of jeans from the kind worth obsessing over. Then there are the pairs that somehow get better the further they travel. Secondhand becomes thirdhand, thirdhand becomes fourth. Knees get blown out, hems get frayed, and repairs become repairs of repairs over time. Add to the list: patches, sashiko stitching, and boro-inspired mending that ultimately turn what started as a pair of regular ol' jeans into something completely its own.Now, finding those pairs is another story. Unless you’re the kind of denim-head who can spot a manufacturer from its stitching, date a pair by its hardware, or tell when a brand quietly changed its fit, vintage shopping online can become an expensive game of squinting at measurements, pulling the trigger, and praying they fit when they arrive.But what if you could buy your vintage brand new? Enter NEEDBY VINTAGE. Founded by Tsuyoshi Kikushima, whose resume includes True Religion, RED CARD, and Rag & Bone, NEEDBY approaches denim less as reproduction than reconstruction. The brand operates within Okayama Prefecture, home to Kojima — widely recognized as the birthplace of domestically produced Japanese jeans and now one of the world’s most closely watched centers for denim manufacturing and processing.That history matters because NEEDBY isn’t simply making new jeans look old. As the brand puts it, it “does not imitate ageing — it designs it.” Washing and distressing become part of the design process itself, layering fading, paint, repairs, and panels of contrasting denim with enough precision that the finished product feels less like a factory-made vintage reproduction and more like a pair that has somehow accumulated several lives before reaching the rack. The first time I saw Arthur Jafa’s "Love Is the Message, The Message Is Death" was in November 2016 at Gavin Brown’s Enterprise in Harlem, just days after the presidential election. Kanye West’s “Ultralight Beam” filled the room while Jafa moved through images of Black life at an almost rapid fire pace that barely gave you time to settle into one. Family footage, athletes, musicians, police violence, famous faces, people I didn’t recognize.I remember the feeling more than any single image. The film had this strange push and pull to it. Something beautiful would sit beside something brutal, something intimate beside something pulled from television. The film was only a few minutes long, but it stayed with me. I thought about that experience again on September 22, walking through the media preview of Arthur Jafa: I Am Tony at the New Museum.The show spans the museum’s third and fourth floors and is Jafa’s first U.S. museum survey to bring together the full range of his practice, from film and photography to sculpture, painting and installation. The title comes from the hugely influential jazz drummer Tony Williams and the exhibition includes works like "Love Is the Message" and "The White Album" alongside more recent pieces and new work.One of the collections I spent the most time with were the binders. They’re dense with images Jafa has collected over the years: anonymous family photographs, magazine clippings, advertisements, scans of album covers and historical material. Marvin Gaye, MF DOOM, and more portraits that feel culturally familiar and others that look like they were dug up from a time capsule.One spread had a clipping of…

a4977d3fa4:94ee67507c42b920.title: 10 Era-Defining Figures to Know From Sotheby’s Next Hong Kong Sale
a4977d3fa4:94ee67507c42b920.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:94ee67507c42b920.summary: The human form is never simply a story of flesh and blood. Throughout human history, artists have turned to the body to make sense of the era and the social world that produced it — from war and alienation to consumerism, identity, and desire. As Sotheby’s Hong Kong readies its Modern and Contemporary Art auction season, we’re taking a look at the stories behind 10 works from the last century of art history.Tradition Meets Modernity (1910s–1950s)The turn of the 20th century wasn’t about throwing the rules out completely, as it was fracturing them. Across Asia, artists blended Eastern and Western philosophies, styles, and techniques to reckon with a new kind of modernity. For Chinese painter Sanyu, that meant bringing the body back to its essential elements. In “Nude, Hugging Knees, Viewed from the Front I” (1950s), anatomy disappears into abstraction, in a figure defined by sparse lines and calligraphic curves. Mai Trung Thu’s “Mélodie” (1950) takes a more nostalgic approach. Working in France at the time, the artist rendered the musician through restrained color and intimate composition to evoke a sense of longing for home, memory, and connection across oceans.“Woman in Chemise” (1925–28) by Zenzaburo Kojima exhibits a similar style of play. An estimated 1.6 million people turned out for the show, officially making it the biggest crowd ever assembled for a solo DJ set.The scale is staggering. Harris performed from a carnival float that rolled through Rua da Consolação in central São Paulo, effectively converting one of the city's main arteries into a sprawling open-air dancefloor as crowds filled the surrounding streets. Across the set, he ran through a string of his biggest global singles, including “This Is What You Came For,” “One Kiss,” “I Need Your Love” and “We Found Love.”Harris matched the occasion with a fitting look, pulling on a Brazil shirt numbered "00" with "Calvinho" printed across the back as he played from the moving platform. The nod to Brazilian football and carnival culture made the moment feel native to the city rather than an imported spectacle, and it marked his first return to Brazil in more than a decade.Guinness World Records has formally recognized the São Paulo show, citing the 1.6 million figure in confirming the title. "Calvin Harris has spent years creating music that brings people together, so to see that reflected on this scale is really quite remarkable," said Will Munford, Official Guinness World Records Adjudicator. a4977d3fa4:646520f6b934fcb2.title: Nike Dresses Up This Air Force 1 Low in Snakeskin and a Trio of Gold Charms
a4977d3fa4:646520f6b934fcb2.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:646520f6b934fcb2.summary: Name: Nike Air Force 1 Low “Gold Charms”Colorway: White/Metallic Gold/WhiteSKU: IZ8908-100MSRP: $125 USDRelease Date: TBCThe Air Force 1 Low is the latest canvas for Nike’s growing charm obsession, pairing the silhouette's signature all-white leather with a snakeskin-textured Swoosh and a set of removable golden trinkets. It's a restrained update on paper that leans on its accessories to do the talking.The foundation stays true to the AF1 blueprint, built on the clean white leather upper that made the model a wardrobe staple. The tweak comes at the Swoosh, rendered here in a tan finish and wrapped in a snakeskin texture that adds a tactile, slightly exotic edge without disrupting the neutral palette. The effect is deliberately understated, setting a quiet base for the flashier hardware.That hardware is the real hook. A trio of golden charms dangles from the laces, made up of a miniature Swoosh, a star, and an Air Force 1 emblem. The cluster attaches by a lobster claw, so it can be repositioned anywhere the clasp fits or pulled off entirely and used to dress up something beyond the shoe. It's a small detail with outsized flexibility, turning a fixed design element into something wearers can rearrange on a whim.The charm treatment also fits into a bigger pattern for Nike, which has increasingly leaned on removable accessories across its women's footwear as an easy route to personalization. The Air Force 1 is a natural fit for the approach: its simple, roomy construction leaves plenty of space for decorative flourishes without tipping into clutter, letting the extras register as intentional rather than busy. d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.title: The Trouble With the Nuclear-AI Analogy
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.author: Christopher LaRoche, Ankit Panda
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.summary: In humanity’s quest to constrain the dangers from fast-advancing artificial intelligence, many have looked to the most revolutionary technology that preceded it: nuclear weapons. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has called artificial intelligence “far more dangerous than nukes.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who assigns The Making of the Atomic Bomb to employees and has likened himself to the Manhattan Project scientist Leo Szilard, describes the most powerful AI models as “weaponizable nuclear materials.” When asked how a technology such as AI can be regulated, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman often references the world’s nuclear materials watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency. Even the director of the CIA, John Ratcliffe, has made the same comparison.These comparisons capture real parallels. Like nuclear weapons, frontier AI is powerful and hard to control. Like nuclear technology, it can be used for good or for ill. And like the Cold War arms race, the race for AI breakthroughs may reorder the global balance of power. The nuclear analogy, then, seems to offer a blueprint for how to effectively govern a promising but potentially dangerous technology such as AI.

fc066e842d:f89f05c8bc834f39.title: Reversibility as a Factor of Production: A General Theory of the Economics of Error
fc066e842d:f89f05c8bc834f39.author: YAHYA, Ould Amar
fc066e842d:f89f05c8bc834f39.summary: What the Article proposes. All growth is born of trials — projects launched, firms founded, techniques attempted — and most trials fail. What each society does with those failures is, this Article argues, the most decisive and least measured variable in economics. Where honest failure leaves its author with his capabilities, his assets and his reputation, people try often, learn fast and prosper; where failure destroys — perpetual debt, stigma, disqualification, personal ruin — the most rational agents stop trying, and the economy dies out for want of experiments. The Article gives this intuition a complete theoretical body: it introduces the “reversibility coefficient ρ, ” the fraction of his capabilities an agent retains after an honest failure, elevates it to a factor of production on a par with capital and labor, and endows it with a law of formation, a geometry, theorems and an instrument of measurement. A pharmaceutical laboratory screens ten thousand molecules to retain a single one for a drug; the 9, 999 failures are not losses but precious information — each closes a path, sharpens the map and brings the medicine closer, to the point that laboratories parse their competitors’ failures line by line. The Article asks that the economy as a whole treat error as the laboratory treats it — a raw material of discovery — and not as a punitive society treats it, where a mistake closes the future to whoever makes it. The thesis holds that development begins neither with savings nor with capital goods, but when falling ceases to mean being destroyed. Why reversibility truly is a factor of production. Economic science admits as a factor of production any magnitude that meets three criteria: it is scarce and costly to produce; its increase raises output, other factors held constant; and it accumulates and depreciates like a stock. Reversibility passes all three tests. It is productive: with capital, labor and talent held identical, ρ governs both the number of trials…

fc066e842d:dea68a113565c652.title: Towards a dynamic conceptualisation of the Regional Innovation System: The Systemic Knowledge Network Continuum
fc066e842d:dea68a113565c652.author: Nick Clifton
fc066e842d:dea68a113565c652.summary: The Regional Innovation Systems (RIS) framework explains regional innovation performance primarily through structural conditions and external knowledge flows. While this perspective has generated influential typologies and policy models, it offers limited insight into how RISs emerge and transform from within. This paper advances a dynamic perspective that conceptualises RIS development as a continuum from fragmented interaction to systemic integration. We argue that generative network mechanisms and systemic dimensions co-evolve recursively, enabling or constraining the formation of integrated RISs. By shifting attention from static structures to self-reinforcing dynamics, the framework provides a foundation for understanding RIS formation, transformation, and reversibility, and suggests a more adaptive, mechanism-oriented approach to policy.

fc066e842d:24d84e140192b3ce.title: Discovering Green: The Role of Organizational and Network Embeddedness in the Shift Toward Sustainability Research
fc066e842d:24d84e140192b3ce.author: Tom Broekel
fc066e842d:24d84e140192b3ce.summary: This study examines researchersâ€™ diversification into sustainability research, distinguishing between initial entry and subsequent engagement intensity. While the existing literature emphasises individual-level drivers, we argue that such diversification is also shaped by organisational and relational contexts. Using bibliometric data from the University of Stavanger, Norway, we show that network distance to sustainability-active colleagues is a key predictor: researchers who are structurally closer to engaged peers are more likely to enter the field and deepen their involvement. By contrast, department- and faculty-level sustainability activities show weaker, more context-dependent associations, with department-level effects disappearing once network variables are included. The findings highlight the importance of intra-organisational knowledge networks for sustainability-oriented research transitions.

fc066e842d:39259eaee8076066.title: Diffusion of tacit knowledge in a company: a mathematical model based on diffusion on graphs
fc066e842d:39259eaee8076066.author: Andrzej Buszko
fc066e842d:39259eaee8076066.summary: This article is devoted to the process of diffusing tacit knowledge. This intangible asset has proven crucial for achieving a competitive advantage among market-oriented companies. A novel model of tacit knowledge diffusion is presented, employing the concept of heat diffusion from physics. Furthermore, graph theory and the dynamics it defines are utilized. We defined a Tacit Knowledge Transfer Graph that encodes data from questionnaires. It enables us to identify employees' learning needs, allowing for the planning of classes within the same period, such as a day, to schedule them optimally. Moreover, the model can be used to identify employees with high knowledge demands. The application is not limited to companies; a simple example of planning classes in a school/university is provided. The presented model can help with optimal scheduling, enhance operational efficiency, and improve talent management within the company. It can also identify risks associated with critical sources of knowledge and help improve organizational culture and knowledge management policy.

fc066e842d:e0ba07a8dbabc318.title: Corporate research and value creation in Peru
fc066e842d:e0ba07a8dbabc318.author: Iglesias-Osores, Sebastian
fc066e842d:e0ba07a8dbabc318.summary: This working paper develops a conceptual and contextual framework for understanding corporate research in Peru as a value-creation capability rather than as an activity mainly induced by public grants or tax incentives. The central argument is that public innovation funds and tax benefits can accelerate business innovation, but they cannot substitute for the internal routines through which firms learn, document, protect, and capture value from knowledge. Drawing on the resource-based view, the knowledge-based theory of the firm, absorptive capacity, dynamic capabilities, open innovation, technological capability accumulation in emerging economies, and the appropriability literature, the paper proposes an integrated pathway linking corporate research, structured learning, firm-specific know-how, appropriability decisions, innovation capability, and economic value capture. The argument is situated in the Peruvian context through indicators of low R&D intensity, public information on Law No. 30309, patenting evidence, and sectoral illustrative cases. The paper contributes by reframing public innovation instruments as levers of pre-existing capabilities rather than substitutes for strategy, and by offering a practical maturity framework for managers seeking to transform research activities into intangible assets, technical reputation, and new sources of income.

5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.title: Presidential Address: Neighborhood Effects and Missing Markets for Opportunity
5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.author: info@aeaweb.org (Lawrence F. Katz1 1 Harvard University (email: lkatz@harvard.edu))
5b51167fb0:140613fdcd625616.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3197-3222 Abstract Experimental and quasi-experimental studies show that childhood neighborhoods have substantial causal impacts on children's adult earnings and other long-term socioeconomic outcomes. Several market failures are likely to lead to excessive residential segregation by parental income and to an undersupply of mixed-income neighborhoods. Missing markets for opportunity originate in capital market imperfections for borrowing on children's future earnings, neighbor spillovers, behavioral biases, and housing search frictions. Customized housing mobility services combined with subsidized housing vouchers can help low-income families move to higher-opportunity areas. Place-based policies that create mixed-income neighborhoods appear to increase long-term outcomes for less-advantaged children. (JEL I12, I32, I38, J13, J15, R23, R38)

5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.title: Contextually Private Mechanisms
5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.author: info@aeaweb.org (Andreas Haupt1 and Zoë Hitzig2 1 Stanford Digital Economy Lab (email: h4upt@stanford.edu) 2 Harvard Society of Fellows (email: zhitzig@g.harvard.edu))
5b51167fb0:efb7cbbe3071ae07.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3223-3262 Abstract A designer employs a dynamic protocol to elicit private information. Protocols produce a set of contextual privacy violations—information learned that may be superfluous given the context. A protocol is maximally contextually private if there is no protocol that produces a proper subset of the violations it produces, while implementing the choice rule. Contextual privacy violations arise when a choice rule makes some agents collectively, but not individually, pivotal. In auctions, designing for contextual privacy requires choosing an initial question posed to each agent and the order for querying agents. Ascending-join protocols are maximally contextually private for k-item Vickrey auctions. (JEL D44, D82)

5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.title: Manipulation-Robust Prediction
5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.author: info@aeaweb.org (Daniel Björkegren1, Joshua E. Blumenstock2 and Samsun Knight3 1 Columbia University (email: dan@bjorkegren.com) 2 UC Berkeley (email: jblumenstock@berkeley.edu) 3 University of…
5b51167fb0:1a15b1cd2416f9fe.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3263-3293 Abstract An increasing number of decisions are guided by machine learning algorithms. But when consequential decisions are encoded in algorithms, individuals may strategically alter their behavior to achieve desired outcomes. This paper develops an empirical approach that adjusts decision algorithms to anticipate manipulation. By explicitly modeling incentives to manipulate, our approach produces decision rules that are stable under manipulation, even when the rules are fully transparent. We stress-test this approach through a large field experiment in Kenya. When implemented, linear strategy-robust decision rules outperform standard linear models such as LASSO. (JEL C45, C93, D12, D91, G51, O12, O16)

5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.title: Risk-Sharing Tests and Covariate Shocks: Drought, Floods, and Pests in Uganda
5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.author: info@aeaweb.org (Ethan Ligon1 1 University of California, Berkeley (email: ligon@berkeley.edu))
5b51167fb0:a1ffa58aef64f33d.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3294-3329 Abstract Efficient risk sharing implies a simple factor structure for marginal utilities of expenditure (MUEs): Pareto weights divided by a common price. The standard approach infers MUEs from total expenditures, implicitly assuming homothetic preferences, unitary income elasticities, and identical price elasticities. Risk-sharing tests using total expenditures work for idiosyncratic shocks (budgets change, but not prices), but not “covariate” shocks (prices change). I describe all preferences that permit one to infer MUEs from expenditures and estimate nonhomothetic MUEs to test whether covariate shocks are shared efficiently in Uganda. This delivers sensible results; the standard approach suggests that droughts, floods, and pests are beneficial. (JEL D12, D81, O12, O13, Q12)

5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.title: Optimal Public Transportation Networks: Evidence from the World's Largest Bus Rapid Transit System in Jakarta
5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.author: info@aeaweb.org (Gabriel Kreindler1, Arya Gaduh2, Tilman Graff3, Rema Hanna4 and Benjamin A. Olken5 1 Harvard University (email: gkreindler@g.harvard.edu) 2 University of Arkansas (email:…
5b51167fb0:797852c7470100e9.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3330-3379 Abstract Designing public transport networks involves trade-offs between coverage, service frequency, and direct service. We use the expansion of the bus system in Jakarta, Indonesia, to study these trade-offs. We analyze how new direct connections, changes in bus travel time, and wait-time reductions affect bus ridership and aggregate flows and estimate a transit network demand model by matching the route launch events. Commuters in Jakarta are 2–3 times more sensitive to wait time than bus time and inattentive to long routes. We develop a flexible framework to characterize optimal networks. A less concentrated network would increase ridership and commuter welfare. (JEL L92, L98, O18, R41, R42, R48)

5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.title: Corporate Tax Cuts, Firm Growth, and Workers' Earnings
5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.author: info@aeaweb.org (Patrick J. Kennedy1, Christine L. Dobridge2, Paul Landefeld3 and Jacob Mortenson4 1 UCLA, NBER, and JCT (email: pkennedy@econ.ucla.edu) 2 Federal Reserve Board (email:…
5b51167fb0:07fc24e40491cd16.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3380-3422 Abstract We study the effects of the largest corporate income tax cut in US history on firms and workers. To identify causal effects, we use employer-employee matched tax records and event studies comparing similarly sized firms in the same industry that faced divergent tax changes due to their preexisting legal status. Tax cuts cause increases in firms' investment, sales, profits, employment, and payrolls, with earnings gains concentrated among highly paid workers. In the short run, 87 percent of private income gains flow to the top 10 percent of the income distribution. (JEL D22, D31, G31, H25, H32, J23, L25)

5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.title: Marriage, Fertility, and Cultural Integration in Italy
5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.author: info@aeaweb.org (Alberto Bisin1 and Giulia Tura2 1 New York University (email: alberto.bisin@nyu.edu) 2 LUISS University (email: gtura@luiss.it))
5b51167fb0:3ee043839f43fb4e.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3423-3463 Abstract We study cultural integration as an equilibrium outcome of marital matching along cultural and education lines and intrahousehold investment decisions regarding fertility and cultural socialization. Our model allows us to identify cultural-ethnic-group-specific investment parameters and spousal preferences for marital matching. Structural estimates reveal a strong demand to preserve cultural identity on the part of immigrants and limited acceptance of the immigrants' cultural diversity on the part of natives. Furthermore, these estimates reveal a substantial heterogeneity of the parental value of children's education across cultures. Nonetheless, our estimates simulate substantial—though heterogeneous—cultural integration rates across immigrant groups. (JEL D13, J12, J13, J15, Z13)

5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.title: Defying Distance? The Provision of Medical Services in the Digital Age
5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.author: info@aeaweb.org (Amanda Dahlstrand1 1 University of Zurich (email: amanda.dahlstrand@econ.uzh.ch))
5b51167fb0:26e7d435f0796a13.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3464-3509 Abstract Digital platforms reduce geographic frictions, enabling better matching between service providers and users. I quantify reallocation gains in Swedish online health care, using nationwide time-conditional random assignment between patients and physicians. Matching high-risk patients with doctors effective at reducing Emergency Room visits lowers such visits by 4.4 percent (SE 1.3); reallocations also reduce Counter-Guideline antibiotics by 3.1 percent (1.4). I find limited trade-offs in matching; horizontal differentiation among doctors and varied patient needs allow improvement in multiple outcomes simultaneously. Efficiency-enhancing reallocations also affect equity. The findings highlight the potential for care reorganization aligning provider heterogeneity with patient needs when geographic constraints are lifted. (JEL C78, H51, I11, I13, I14, I18)

5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.title: The Environmental Bias of Corporate Income Taxation
5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.author: info@aeaweb.org (Luigi Iovino1, Thorsten Martin2 and Julien Sauvagnat3 1 Bocconi University (email: luigi.iovino@unibocconi.it) 2 Frankfurt School of Finance and Management (email: t.martin@fs.de) 3…
5b51167fb0:221f12c25326ebda.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3510-3551 Abstract We study the relationship between corporate income taxation and carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in the United States. We show CO2-intensive firms benefit more from the tax advantage of debt and pay lower income taxes on their capital income. Building on these new facts, we provide evidence that a cut in the corporate income tax rate leads to a larger expansion of clean firms. We develop a multisector general equilibrium model that accounts for our evidence and quantify the impact of corporate tax reforms on aggregate emissions. A policy that eliminates the tax advantage of debt could reduce aggregate emissions without affecting GDP. (JEL D22, G32, H25, H32, Q52, Q54, Q58)

5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.title: Rationing by Race
5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.author: info@aeaweb.org (Manasvini Singh1 and Atheendar Venkataramani2 1 Carnegie Mellon University and NBER (email: msingh01@cmu.edu) 2 University of Pennsylvania and NBER (email:…
5b51167fb0:273a7079633c9788.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3552-3585 Abstract We document how deepening resource scarcity results in rationing on the basis of race in a high-stakes setting: health care. Using detailed, time stamped data on 107,000 inpatient admissions to a large health system, we find that in-hospital mortality increases for Black but not White patients as hospitals reach capacity. These findings are not explained by differential patient selection. We identify rationing by wait times as a mechanism, documenting that sicker Black patients wait longer for care than healthier White patients at almost all capacity levels. Text analysis of unstructured clinical notes reveals rationing of provider effort as another mechanism. (JEL I11, I12, I14, J15)

5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.title: Intergenerational Impacts of Secondary Education: Experimental Evidence from Ghana
5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.author: info@aeaweb.org (Esther Duflo1, Pascaline Dupas2, Elizabeth Spelke3 and Mark Walsh4 1 MIT and Collège de France (email: eduflo@mit.edu) 2 Princeton University (email: pdupas@princeton.edu) 3 Harvard…
5b51167fb0:b142b734d632b9cc.summary: American Economic Review 116 (9): 3586-3621 Abstract We provide experimental evidence on the intergenerational impacts of secondary education subsidies in a low-income context, leveraging a randomized controlled trial and 15-year longitudinal follow-up. Secondary school scholarships delay fertility, reduce unwanted pregnancies, and change partner selection. Under-one mortality is reduced by half. We also document cognitive development gains of 0.24 standard deviations of test scores by age five among children of female scholarship recipients. Means-tested secondary school scholarships are a high-return investment, with a conservatively estimated US$4.1 in benefits for each US$1 the policy would cost the government in the long run. (JEL H52, I12, I21, I26, J13, J16, O15)

21113a7a19:603639c33f400b49.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:603639c33f400b49.summary: The not-so-secret secret of building a good school is to have good students. And sometimes that can lead to conflicts between the desire to build better school systems to serve children in the aggregate, and the desire to put your child in the best school for him or her. A NYT columnist talks about this, writing "In New York, a combination of housing segregation and “academic” sorting, called school choice , that begins as early as pre-K means most Black students — even middle-class ones — are forced to attend racially segregated schools with high rates of poverty." (emphasis added) In Fighting for Every Black Child, Did I Betray My Own? A decade ago, I made a decision about my daughter’s education that I hoped would challenge New York City’s separate and unequal school system. Now 16, she thinks I made the wrong choice. By Nikole Hannah-Jones ####### On a somewhat related note, when I speak to prospective PhD students who are visiting universities after being admitted to multiple PhD programs, I encourage them to talk to the graduate students already there, and discover how happy, productive, and collaborative they are. A good PhD program is one where you learn a lot by collaborating with your fellow students in study and research.

"I founded Organize, a nonprofit making it easier to register to become an organ donor. In 2015, Organize was selected for a role embedded inside the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, which put us on the radar of whistle-blowers. I soon became inundated with allegations from people working inside the organ donation industry who felt they had nowhere else to turn. "I know as well as anyone that organ donation saves lives — over 40,000 annually in the United States in recent years. But I was stunned to learn that organ procurement organizations — the federal contractors that coordinate organ donation from the deceased — that made those transplants possible were routinely violating ethical standards and putting patients at risk. "I heard allegations of negligence and financial fraud, including industry executives’ billing taxpayers for joyrides on private jets meant to transport organs; of organizations performing unnecessary procedures as part of a scheme to overbill Medicare. (Organ procurement organizations are nonprofits, but that doesn’t mean they aren’t trying to maximize financial reimbursements.) I’ve heard of poorer Americans waiting to receive organs passed over in favor of wealthier ones. 21113a7a19:8562b73267220857.title: Experimenting on the psychology of LLMs
21113a7a19:8562b73267220857.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:8562b73267220857.summary: As LLMs become increasingly important, we're starting to see experiments that explore their psychology. (I expect that Susan Calvin, who was Isaac Asimov's fictional robopsychologist from the1950 short story collection I Robot , will soon have scientists following in her footsteps.) Note that experiments intended to explore A.I. psychology need not necessarily resemble those intended to explore human psychology. Here's an example, from the journal Artificial Intelligence and the Law: Human realignment: An empirical study of LLMs as legal decision-aids in moral dilemmas by Christoph Engel · Yoan Hermstrüwer · Alison Kim Abstract: Recent advances in AI make it conceivable to delegate legal decision-making to machines, or to enhance human adjudication through AI assistance. Using classic normative conflicts — the trolley problem and comparable moral dilemmas — as a proof of concept, we examine the alignment between AI legal reasoning and human judgment. In our baseline experiment, we find a pronounced mismatch between decisions made by GPT and those of human subjects. This misalignment raises substantive concerns for AI-powered legal decision-aids. We investigate whether explicit normative guidance can address this misalignment, with mixed results. GPT-3.5 is susceptible to such intervention, but frequently refuses to decide when faced with a moral dilemma. GPT-4 is outright utilitarian, and essentially ignores the instruction to decide on deontological grounds. GPT-o3-mini faithfully implements this instruction, but is unwilling to balance deontological and utilitarian concerns if instructed to do so. We replicate the experiment with four LLMs from different providers. Claude-sonnet-4.6 comes closest to human respondents. Gemini-2.5-flash-lite is most sensitive to normative instructions. 21113a7a19:c56640781616b6c7.title: Xenotransplants will substitute for dialysis before they replace human kidney transplants
21113a7a19:c56640781616b6c7.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:c56640781616b6c7.summary: Transplants of organs from genetically modified pigs to humans is making progress, but pig organs haven't yet survived long enough to be a viable substitute for human organs. Kidneys are a good experimental organ to work with, because when the pig organ fails, the patient can go back on dialysis (and continue to wait for a deceased-donor organ transplant). But if pig organs can last long enough, they might replace dialysis. The first pig-organ recipient to go straight to a human organ transplant has now been reported, in a press release accompanying the case report. Below are both the press release and the case report. Patient Who Received Pig Kidney Becomes First To Progress to Human Kidney Transplant Study shows xenotransplantation can serve as a bridge for patients with end-stage kidney disease By MASS GENERAL BRIGHAM COMMUNICATIONS September 3, 2026 Riella L, Borges T, Rosales I et al. Porcine kidney xenotransplantation as a bridge to allotransplantation: a first-in-human study The Lancet, 2026; "This case shows that porcine kidney xenotransplantation can provide prolonged renal support and be discontinued without clinically significant allosensitisation or zoonotic infection. Early cellular rejection resolved with treatment, whereas later graft failure was associated with microvascular injury progressing to thrombotic microangiopathy despite a negative donor-specific crossmatch, supporting the possibility that mechanisms beyond conventional antibody-mediated rejection contributed to late graft injury. Kidney xenotransplantation has the potential to provide prolonged dialysis-free support while also serving as a bridge to subsequent human allotransplantation ."

21113a7a19:2c743f5c371780f9.title: How to Get Away with Merger in a Dialysis Duopoly by T.G. Wollman
21113a7a19:2c743f5c371780f9.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:2c743f5c371780f9.summary: Here's a paper featured by Microeconomic Insights, which shows that in the highly concentrated dialysis market, in which prices are mostly federally regulated, mergers reduce competition on quality. Thomas G. Wollmann: How to Get Away with Merger: Stealth Consolidation and Its Effects on US Dialysis "This paper studies premerger notification of US dialysis acquisitions from 1996 to 2017. Like many industries, dialysis has consolidated rapidly. During this period, thousands of facilities changed ownership, yet only half were reported to federal antitrust authorities. Unlike most industries, dialysis prices are mostly set by the government, so acquisitions of rival facilities reduce the incentive to compete on quality. Since patients are often already in poor health, preventing stealth consolidation could save lives. The study combines data on market structure, antitrust enforcement, and patient health. I begin by describing patterns in the data. Next, I estimate a structural model of dialysis competition, enforcement, and agency costs. Finally, I use the estimates to predict what would have happened had all dialysis mergers proposed during the study period been reportable. Three main findings emerge. Premerger notification is critical to effective antitrust enforcement. All else equal, exemption reduces the likelihood of enforcement by about 90%. Exempt acquisitions that concentrate ownership degrade quality, as evidenced by higher postmerger hospitalization and mortality rates. The benefits of expanding premerger notification exceed the costs by orders of magnitude. This reflects the deterrence effect of antitrust enforcement (i.e., rivals won’t try to merge if they know their deal will be blocked) as well as the efficiency of the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), which polices billions of dollars of dialysis transactions with very few resources."

21113a7a19:48bf1e536ed66724.title: Three takeaways on Moral Economics, with Lynn Thoman
21113a7a19:48bf1e536ed66724.author: Al Roth (noreply@blogger.com)
21113a7a19:48bf1e536ed66724.summary: Lynn Thoman and I discuss three takeaways from Moral Economics (and hers are different than mine): You can listen here: Why Doing the “Right Thing” Can Make Everything Worse and you can watch as well as listen here: "What can we do when doing the morally “right” thing produces worse outcomes? And what if some of society’s strongest moral instincts are preventing us from solving problems we all agree are terrible? Alvin Roth is a Stanford professor and Nobel Prize-winning economist whose work has helped redesign real-world systems, including kidney exchanges and the way doctors are matched with hospitals. His new book, Moral Economics, tackles a harder category of problems: markets and behaviors we find morally objectionable, even when banning them may create consequences we don’t want. He discusses: Why nearly 100,000 Americans can be waiting for a kidney What prohibitions of alcohol and heroin can teach us What happened when Rhode Island accidentally legalized indoor prostitution Whether paying kidney donors could save lives without creating an ethically unacceptable market Why evidence becomes especially important when reasonable people disagree about morality Whether performance-enhancing drugs could eventually become as ordinary as coffee Some policies sound obviously right when judged by their intentions. But what happens when you judge them by their actual consequences? Roth pushes into the uncomfortable territory between those two questions: when banning something creates a black market, when changing a rule may save more lives than inventing a new technology, and what we should do when the outcome we believe is morally necessary turns out to be something we cannot actually achieve."

21113a7a19:5eca3d944980dd90.summary: I'm always on the lookout for different perspectives on market design, and here's a paper that caught my eye in the ASSA Preliminary Program for the January 2027 meetings in Washington DC. It's in a session called What Economic Models Can and Cannot See: Human Flourishing, Freedom, and the Common Good (B4 ) Hosted by the Association of Christian Economists Can Market Design Make Us More Free? Some Notes on the Use of Experimental Economics from the Perspective of Theological Anthropology by Christina McRorie , Boston College Abstract Although modern thought tends to construe freedom as freedom from constraint or freedom of choice, Catholic theological anthropology has long defined true freedom as the state of being agentially oriented toward the good. As Servais Pinckaers puts it, it is “freedom for,” rather than “freedom from”—specifically, freedom for living in a Christ-like way, which becomes possible as we come to participate in Christ’s character. This perspective suggests that social influences which encourage our growth in character are not only helping us become more good, but also more free. Moreover, because this conception of freedom is not based in autonomy, this remains true even if these formative influences are not chosen by us, and work on us without our awareness. Using this concept of freedom, this paper considers the theological implications of experimental research on prosocial behavior in markets. It appears that certain conditions encourage subjects to act with more fairness, trustworthiness, and even generosity than they might under other conditions. (E.g., when market participants can observe each other’s behavior and communicate, and when the social framing of various options emphasizes values, or at least does not emphasize competition or the threat of loss, among other factors.) 21113a7a19:c3993e442ea33cf6.summary: Here's a recent interview of Axel Ockenfels, about market design. Interview Marc Kley 1. Professor Ockenfels, your work focuses on the design of markets and incentives. How can founders leverage your scientific insights when developing their business models? Every business model is, to some extent, an exercise in incentive and market design, whether founders are aware of it or not. Whoever builds a platform, a pricing scheme or an app decides who can trade with whom, what information they see, and what incentives they face. Market design research offers three lessons for founders. First, details matter: seemingly minor rules can make or break a market. I have seen many systems fail because of seemingly innocuous design mistakes. Second, behavior matters: people reciprocate, care about fairness, are loss averse, and are quickly overwhelmed by complexity. Third, testing matters: experiments are the wind tunnel of market design and the gold standard for finding out what works and what does not. ... 4. In your opinion, which major societal challenge could be solved more effectively if we designed markets, platforms, and incentives more intelligently? Almost any. Take climate change. It is often framed as a moral problem, but at its core it is a cooperation problem: everyone benefits if emissions fall, yet each country, company and individual prefers others to bear the cost. A uniform carbon price would steer billions of everyday decisions toward climate protection without micromanaging any of them. Not less importantly, our research shows that carbon pricing facilitates international negotiations built on reciprocity, which can stabilize cooperation where unilateral pledges fail. A similar logic creates value elsewhere: kidney exchange programs save lives, well-designed electricity markets keep the energy transition affordable, and clever matching systems allocate school places more fairly. 2f5fdda6a0:e478390341646eb1.title: Debt and Taxes: The Role of Tax Avoidance
2f5fdda6a0:e478390341646eb1.author: Brok, Peter
2f5fdda6a0:e478390341646eb1.summary: Empirically, the effect of corporate tax rates on leverage has been smaller than expected based on trade-off theory. In this article, I show that tax avoidance functions as a non-debt tax shield, reducing the benefits of the debt tax shield. I find that higher tax rates cause higher non-debt tax avoidance, which crowds out the debt tax shield. Moreover, I show that the strength of the relationship between debt and tax rates depends on the level of tax avoidance. A 1-standard-deviation higher tax rate implies 2.8% higher leverage for low tax avoidance firms, but has a negative effect for high tax avoidance firms.

2f5fdda6a0:4b5e113d64f964b5.title: Women in Politics: The Effect on Board Diversity
2f5fdda6a0:4b5e113d64f964b5.author: Pareek, Ankur
2f5fdda6a0:4b5e113d64f964b5.summary: We use a sharp regression discontinuity design (RDD) to show that victories by women candidates in close House, Senate, and gubernatorial elections lead to an increase in female directors in firms located in the candidates’ districts. The causal effect is higher when the media coverage of the woman candidate is higher, when voter turnout is high, and when firms have more local directors and local institutional investors. The heterogeneous regression discontinuity (RD) effects suggest that electoral wins may influence local gender norms and firms’ board diversity through multiple channels, including conveying majority views on gender-related social norms, increasing exposure to exemplar women, and facilitating learning about women’s different but effective leadership styles. The evidence suggests a potential spillover effect from women’s political leadership to the corporate world.

2f5fdda6a0:f1502a2b77f8673c.title: Climate-Triggered Institutional Price Pressure: Does It Affect Firms’ Cost of Equity?
2f5fdda6a0:f1502a2b77f8673c.author: Xue, Cheng
2f5fdda6a0:f1502a2b77f8673c.summary: We document that climate-triggered institutional portfolio rebalancing affects S&P 500 firms’ cost of equity through climate change price pressure (CCPP). Using a demand-based asset pricing framework, we estimate firm-level CCPP from physical and transition exposures over 2005–2021. A one-standard-deviation intensification of CCPP raises the cost of equity by up to 6% of its average, with banks and insurers as the main drivers. Yet firms do not subsequently improve environmental performance, indicating that the statistically significant effect of CCPP on cost of equity is ineffective to alter corporate behavior. Our CCPP metrics can help policymakers and investors design targeted environmental strategies.

2f5fdda6a0:47ac36e8dc02670f.title: Do Shareholder Leverage Constraints Affect Debtholders?
2f5fdda6a0:47ac36e8dc02670f.author: Zhang, Lei
2f5fdda6a0:47ac36e8dc02670f.summary: We examine the relationship between shareholder leverage constraints and corporate risk-taking, focusing on its impact on debtholders. Our findings show that mutual fund leverage constraints are related to more risk-taking activities of portfolio companies, inducing higher credit risk and greater risk-shifting concerns for the firms’ debtholders. In response, the debtholders raise borrowing costs and tighten lending conditions. These effects intensify for firms facing higher levels of conflict between debtholders and shareholders and when mutual funds exert greater influence over firms. Econometric analyses, including instrumental variable specifications and asset management company mergers, support a causal interpretation.
